analysis:
Examined both test excerpts, release-workflow metadata and both patch hunks against the canonical definition index and selected details. The only test behavior change is an explicit synthetic GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=1 in .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py:930; it stabilizes the fixture under runner reruns without changing the production rerun gate. The surrounding tests separately exercise attempt=2 rejection (953–962), permission checks (1153–1158), coverage/citation validation, retained findings, accounting stops, bounded repairs and content-free diagnostics. These assertions are not proof of the omitted implementations.
.github/workflows/release-provider.yml:239–242 pins qualify-sdk to production compilation defaults. The build job retains its resolved release environment (patch head 183); its other change is explanatory text. No changed signing, publication, release registration, permissions or serving-authorization control is visible. Considered artifact identity/qualification contracts (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054): selecting production defaults for tests alone does not establish a trust escalation or qualification bypass. No supplied change modifies prompt encryption, key custody, cache isolation (T-041), native inference, fan control or add-on boundaries.
No concrete regression is supported. Integration should correlate the qualification job with any supplied Package.swift or artifact-qualification changes to ensure test defaults are not mistaken for evidence about a differently compiled artifact. Full workflow, package environment selection and scanner implementations are outside this source excerpt's coverage; no deployment or full-audit conclusion is made.
